programme.title: Engine Power
programme.desc: We work on the Triple Threat Camaro... and play at the OSCR drag race in Bowling Green, KY.

programme.title: Detroit Muscle
programme.desc: Our 1971 Chevy Caprice, Project Fat Stack, ROARS to life after almost a year of work. Tommy and Peyton give the nitty gritty on exhaust installation and finish the interior. Fat Stack turns heads in downtown Nashville to the delight of the Broadway crowd.
programme.sub-title: Fat Stack - Part 14: Clean, Mean, and Candy Green

programme.title: Detroit Muscle
programme.desc: Detail oriented -Tommy and Joel team up with some old friends to tackle the grime and shine up a late model Charger.

programme.title: Music City Trucks
programme.desc: We take one of the most sought after vehicles - a true old-school '74 Ford Bronco, and strip it down to the chassis to bring it back to life, ultimately deciding on building it back up to an actual all-new dream machine...piece by piece.
programme.sub-title: Building a Dream '74 Bronco From the Ground Up

programme.title: Carcass
programme.desc: We bring our C1500 Abandoned Chevy back into the shop for an easy to install EFI setup that will allow for more boost and power. Plus we head out to Mid-Ohio Sports Car Course to compete with our Spec Panther race car.
programme.sub-title: Adding An EFI Setup To The C1500 Chevy

programme.title: XOR - Xtreme Off-Road
programme.desc: We're getting the rear racing suspension installed in our 2002 Ford Ranger!

programme.title: Detroit Muscle
programme.desc: Our Mustang Cobra project "Sydewinder" hits the track at the Mid America Ford and Shelby Nationals! 600+Horsepower and set up for the track, the Foxbody beast is loose!
programme.sub-title: Mustang Sydewinder at the Mid America Ford and Shelby Nationals

programme.title: Detroit Muscle
programme.desc: The guys down in Engine Power have finished beefing up our '69 Camaro' s engine with some high-performance parts, now we have to install it and upgrade the drive train so it can hold it's own with today's modern muscle.
programme.sub-title: Squeezing the Heartbeat Of Our '69 Camaro Between the Fenders

programme.title: Engine Power
programme.desc: Mike and Pat stroke a vintage junkyard Ford 390 but an unexpected surprise puts a delay in their progress. Then it's full steam ahead for finding the limit for this big block stump puller
programme.sub-title: Junkyard Ford 390 FE Teardown and Rebuild

programme.title: Detroit Muscle
programme.desc: We take Project Sydewinder to get its suspension setup for the track. Plus, Tommy and Marc get a rare look inside the Indianapolis Motor Speedway Museum Vault.
programme.sub-title: Setting Front End Alignment for the Track on a Mustang Foxbody

programme.title: Carcass
programme.desc: We start tearing into the powertrain of our Datsun 280Z, freshening up the engine and converting the automatic transmission to a sportier manual setup. We'll also take a look at the new Nissan Z!
programme.sub-title: Pulling The L28 Out Of Our 1978 Datsun 280Z Heritage Restomod

programme.title: Detroit Muscle
programme.desc: Interior Decorated - Tommy and Joel cut a rug and freshen up the rest of Fat Stack's interior to match the flashy exterior of their 1971 Chevy Caprice.

programme.title: Detroit Muscle
programme.desc: Tommy and Peyton make a plan of attack to resurrect a 1966 Chevy Nova, a first for the Detroit Muscle shop. After their upscale treatment, this Nova, codenamed Project Starstruck, will be a low, mean, aggressive street machine with killer looks.
programme.sub-title: Basket Case - Rusted, Busted, and Ruined

programme.title: Music City Trucks
programme.desc: The OBS Chevy is in the shop to mock up it's new suspension. We'll have to make a few modifications to the spring pockets before installing our front suspension. In the rear we'll address frame issues before we can add a c-notch to get our rear suspension in place before our chassis heads out to poweder coat.

programme.title: Detroit Muscle
programme.desc: Step by step, we install a new top on our 1966 Pontiac convertible. Plus, a High Performance visit to Las Vegas for LS Fest West.
programme.sub-title: How to Install a Convertible Top

programme.title: Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Live "Crushing It"
programme.desc: Driving a monster truck isn't easy, but Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Live host, Tommy Kane, shows you how, when he gets behind the wheel of a legendary monster truck. Don't miss the action and the behind the scenes look of our Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Live trucks!

programme.title: Engine Power
programme.desc: We just can't stop searching for more power from our Small Block Chevy! It's getting high-octane race fuel, more aggressive timing, and a bigger cam.
programme.sub-title: Will Race Fuel And A Bigger Cam Improve Power On The Chevy 350 Dyno Mule?

programme.title: Truck Tech
programme.desc: With a fully rebuilt 292 straight-six under the hood, we finish up our patina classic in time to put on some road miles, and check out James Otto's '66 C10 built in an entirely different way.

programme.title: Truck Tech
programme.desc: We take apart our 6.6L Duramax from our '11 Denali HD for an upgrade to 1000HP. Plus, we meet a diesel junkie who built a Cummins powered Ford Ranger pocket rocket for the dragstrip.
programme.sub-title: Tearing Down a Duramax to Prep for 1000 HP

programme.title: Truck Tech
programme.desc: There's a new purpose and a new plan for our Chevy K1500. It's the tips and techniques for a traction machine. GM's Greatest All-Wheel-Drive Idea Applied To Our C/K 1500

programme.title: Engine Power
programme.desc: Meet the graduates of SAMTech who have found a home in NHRA racing.
programme.sub-title: Pit Pass at a NHRA Race Weekend

programme.title: Truck Tech
programme.desc: Modifying a Duramax to make 1000 Horsepower starts with a teardown and some machining before the new performance parts are added. Plus Austin mods up the body for a cool clean look.
programme.sub-title: How to Build a 1000HP Diesel Beast

programme.title: Engine Power
programme.desc: Our 460 Big Block Ford is back for its final iteration, where we upgrade it with a weight saving, better flowing induction. We're looking to up the naturally aspirated horsepower before this beast finds its new home. As always, we'll test our improvement on the Engine Dyno.
programme.sub-title: Better Breathing for our Big Block Ford

programme.title: Detroit Muscle
programme.desc: Adding more Stop and Go to our C5 Corvette Z06 for the track. Taking our Z06 to the Corvette proving grounds, now it can handle the track to strut its stuff!
programme.sub-title: Before and After: Z06 Track Test with Bolt-On Upgrades

programme.title: Music City Trucks
programme.desc: The final touches are added to our '95 Chevy S-10 Mini Truck project. Then we hit the open road and see our LOW-Fi lay frame for the first time. This is a MUST SEE show!
programme.sub-title: Low-Fi S-10: We Wrap Up and Lay Frame!

programme.title: Detroit Muscle
programme.desc: Project Street Regal has it's dated vinyl top removed and we add some goodies to the front of our Mustang Project Sydewinder
programme.sub-title: Adding an Air Splitter on a Mustang Cobra Foxbody

programme.title: Carcass
programme.desc: The Caprice Wagon is back in the shop for the rest of its upgrades. Jimmy and Jeremy add a new drivetrain to give our cruiser a boost in horsepower and then we add a few custom touches before taking the whole tribe on a cross town adventure in the Carcass family truckster.

programme.title: Music City Trucks
programme.desc: Project Night shift is back in the shop! The guys install a rebuilt transfer case in our '93 Dodge Diesel Dually. They also plumb in our bigger turbo setup, showing you how to bead roll your tubing to make a secure fit. Plus, they'll show you the tools you'll need make your own brake lines.

programme.title: Engine Power
programme.desc: Today, it's do or die. We connect TWO 496 Big Block Chevy engines to the dyno to find out exactly how much power two of the same engine will make running in tandem!
programme.sub-title: Twin Big Blocks Dyno'd Together Part 2

programme.title: Engine Power
programme.desc: Searching for more power, let's add Nitrous and see what happens when our Chevy small block gets on the bottle!
programme.sub-title: How Much Nitrous for 720HP in a Small Block?

programme.desc: Detail oriented -Tommy and Joel team up with some old friends to tackle the grime and shine up a late model Charger.

programme.title: Wildest Islands
programme.desc: Lying 40km off the east coast of Tanzania in Africa, the Zanzibar Archipelago has been labelled the most exotic island chain in the world. Pristine sands and azure blue sea make it a much loved holiday destination, but bizarre creatures, many of enormous size, also roam the islands. The world's largest crab scales trees in search of coconuts, and clouds of giant bats fill the skies at dusk.

programme.title: Hawaii: Paradise in the Pacific
programme.desc: In episode two we take a look at Maui and Moloka'i. In the middle of the archipelago they form the heart of Hawaii. The second largest island of Hawai'i - Maui - is a true paradise for surfers. Archie Kalepa was one of the first big wave surfers and is still chasing the thrill today. The ukulele represents the sound of the islands like no other instrument. Eric Devine has been building the plucked string instrument for 20 years. In Kula he goes in search of the perfect wood.

programme.title: Nuts About Squirrels
programme.desc: Even in our most urban settings, pretty much all of us know squirrels. They can be divisive charac-ters; some people adore them, offering them food, while others see them as glorified rats. But we can all agree that these are speedy, quirky, and exceptional characters. They also go crazy for nuts. They've conquered most of the globe, from icy tundra to the hottest deserts, developing ingen-ious life skills along the way, from stashing nuts to fighting snakes.

programme.title: Fighting for a Mate
programme.desc: Animals face daily battles to protect themselves and secure the resources they need to survive. Every battle is a trade-off between the risk to health and the prizes awarded to the victors. Each animal fights with a unique set of tools, from display structures and elaborate body language to claws, jaws and antlers. And few fights are as fuelled as those during breeding season; the ultimate trophy for the brave fighter is, of course, a chance to pass on the fighting genes to the next generation.

programme.title: British Garden: Life And Death On Your Lawn
programme.desc: The British back garden is a familiar setting, but underneath the peonies and petunias is a much wilder hidden world, a miniature Serengeti, with beauty and brutality in equal measure. In this 90-minute documentary Chris Packham and a team of wildlife experts spend an entire year exploring every inch of a series of interlinked back gardens in Welwyn Garden City. They want to answer a fundamental question: how much wildlife lives beyond our back doors?

programme.title: Wildest Places: Australia
programme.desc: Wildest Places explores some of the most incredible natural habitats on earth & a diverse range of wildlife.

programme.title: World of the Wild
programme.desc: Lakes and rivers are created by streams high in the mountains. Fresh water springs, rain drawn up as moisture from the oceans, and melting snow all ebb, rush and flow down into our rivers and streams. Streams, rivers and lakes are home to countless animal species. A wide variety of species from insects, to amphibians, repti-les, fish, birds and even mammals are found in rivers, lakes and streams all around the world.

programme.title: World of the Wild
programme.desc: Wildlife that inhabits mountainous regions has be able to survive successfully at high altitudes. Any creature that lives in the mountains must also be able to cope with changing temperatures. Many species of hoofed and herbivorous mammal such as GOATS, DEER, SHEEP AND LLAMAS have adapted well to living high in the mountains and are often found grazing on ledges and on cliff faces. These herbivores in turn attract large predators such as BEARS, COUGARS AND MOUNTAIN LIONS.

programme.title: Our Big Blue Backyard
programme.desc: The top of New Zealand's South Island is a landscape of two halves. To the West, one of the longest natural sandbars on the planet curves protectively around Golden Bay. To the East, mountains sink into the sea, their drowned river valleys forming the Marlborough Sounds. Turbulent currents connect them, both treacherous and full of riches.
programme.sub-title: Top of the South/ Te Tau Ihu

programme.title: History of Life on Earth - Mammal Takeover
programme.desc: With the dinosaurs' passing, a land of opportunity was laid bare for the little mammals that had scampered about their feet.

programme.title: Hidden Spain
programme.desc: Spain is found at the crossroads between the Mediterranean and the Atlantic, resulting in diverse landscapes, ancient cultures and magnificent wildlife.

programme.title: Fight for Territory
programme.desc: Biological instinct is driven by three things: the desire to stay alive, to find food and to breed. But to do all these things, animals first need a home. Out in the wilderness a safe place to call home can be the difference between life and death. A place to secure meals, raise their families and hide from danger. Ideal spots are in short supply and well worth fighting for!

programme.title: Destination Wild - Wild Argentina
programme.desc: Stretching almost 1000 miles, from the jungles of Brazil to the southernmost point of South America, Patagonia's coast is home to some of the natural world's most spectacular animals. Here, a parched desert collides with a powerful ocean, but right along this extreme and hostile coastline, animals battle the elements and each other, in a fight for survival.

programme.title: The Enchanted Forest
programme.desc: To spend a day in the forest, from dawn to dusk, is to bathe in nature. There's enchantment at every turn. Throughout the day the cast of characters in the forest changes, from foraging bears to playing fox cubs, dashing hummingbirds and dancing butterflies. But it's as twilight descends, that the most enchanting side of the forest is revealed. Time to watch a firework display curtesy of fireflies. They are the real magicians of the enchanted forest.

programme.title: Lions Rule
programme.desc: The Lion, Africa's ultimate predator. An essay in power and agility, famed for the cut-throat gang and the killer instinct. Lions are known as the kings of the jungle yet their homeland is an open grassland rather than rainforest. In the African plains prey-rich real estate can be hard to come by, and lions work together to ensure no one claims their territory and usurps their crown.

programme.title: History of Life on Earth - Mammal Takeover
programme.desc: With the dinosaurs' passing, a land of opportunity was laid bare for the little mammals that had scampered about their feet.

programme.title: Wild Uruguay
programme.desc: Uruguay's biodiversity is surprisingly greater than one would expect. We will find out why as we embark on a journey through its ecosystems and landscapes to discover its fauna. Today we know that Uruguay is more than just the outermost edge of the Pampas, as the country holds a range of ecosystems. Within its borders, species of the Pampas come face to face with species of the Atlantic Forest, the Misiones rainforest, and the Chaco forest, giving rise to unexpected encounters.

programme.title: Hannah Goes to Namibia
programme.desc: Hannah runs a health check on two female cheetahs with veterinarian Maaike. She then goes into the wilderness with Naankuse founder Marlice. Together they go in search of the elephant Apollo, which was resettled in the sanctuary. The former "problem" elephant now leads a peaceful life here.

programme.title: Heroes of the Wild Frontiers
programme.desc: Hunting has been a long-standing cultural tradition in the North Eastern India for long. But with the shirking of the forests and endangering of the wildlife, hunting has become unsustainable. But it is not that this has stopped hunting. The architects of Pakke, a 800 sq Kms forest reserve, in the heart of the hunting villages has done a wonderful job of giving protection to the several endemic species here by keeping the forest safe from the hunters.

programme.title: Hannah Goes to Namibia
programme.desc: As soon as she arrives, conservationist Hannah Emde immerses herself in Namibia's wildlife. The first destination of her trip is the world-famous Naankuse Foundation near Windhoek. In addition to a veterinary clinic, the sanctuary includes 85,000 hectares of wilderness, where endangered and rescued animals live.

programme.title: Wild and Alive
programme.desc: On the savannah of southern Africa, rains have turned the land green and lush. It's the time of plenty and for the cast of wild characters here, cashing in is priority number one. From polecat to aardwolf, some of the continent's most seldom seen creatures are out to make the most of the abundance. Some families gorge on the plentiful grasses, while for others there's no such thing as an easy meal, even at this time of year.

programme.title: Hidden Australia
programme.desc: Sometimes called the biggest island on Earth, Australia is a subcontinent of incredible diversity, beauty, danger and downright weirdness.

programme.title: History of Life on Earth - Rise of the Giants
programme.desc: In the great story of life, reptiles were one of the first major players. For 180 million years they ruled the land, seas and skies - this was the rise of the giants.

programme.title: Destination Wild - Wild Europe
programme.desc: The story of Europe's living waters begins at great altitude. Melt waters from the highest snow-capped peaks feed some of the greatest rivers. On their relentless downward journey, streams and rivers have carved through all of Europe's greatest landscapes. Gorges, lakes and wetlands are home to an incredible array of wildlife and seas and oceans have sculpted a coastline of endless variety.

programme.title: March (Nature's Calendar)
programme.desc: As northern forests become carpeted by bluebells and wood anemones, and damp corners become singles bars for frogs and a toads, hailing the first hint of spring sun, South Africa needs a break from the heat, fire season is in full swing, threatening the fynbos and the extraordinary animals living in them. Ground squirrels get inventive to find shade. Gray whales migrate up the Californian coast, passing colonies of sea otters. March is a month of change

programme.title: Migrations - Herds on the Move
programme.desc: Whether driven by the search for food or the simple will to survive, great herd migrations are some of the most spectacular events of the natural world.

programme.title: Heroes of the Wild Frontiers
programme.desc: What seems calm and tranquil may not necessarily be so. Under the tranquility there maybe a vibrant dynamic world and above water there maybe dangers which are lurking at very corner. Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park is one such. In the Andaman Islands a group of 15 islands make up this fragile eco system. Coral, is one of the most productive and endangered wild fauna in the shallow coastal waters.

programme.title: Wildest Survival
programme.desc: Whether by wing, fin or hoof, epic migrations are among nature's most awe-inspiring events. Animals undertake these arduous journeys, for many reasons: to find a mate, to give birth, or to move to new feeding grounds. And danger lurks at every turn. In this episode we discover the lengths they go to in order to survive.

programme.title: Wildest Islands
programme.desc: Lying like a teardrop in the Indian Ocean, Sri Lanka is an island that defies convention. Poised just six degrees above the equator, it's less than 75,000 km sq in size. But it has enough wildlife to rival a continent, and it's all down to its complicated climate and geography.

programme.title: Sexy Beasts
programme.desc: Driven by surging hormones, every creature on the planet, big or small, will do whatever it takes to find and secure a mate. For some this will take the fight of their lives, while others must preen, prance and party their way to success. From one night stands and group sex to lifelong love and unbreakable bonds, when it comes to finding a mate the animal kingdom has it all. The need to breed manifests itself in all sorts of wonderful antics, displays and behaviours.

programme.title: Destination Wild - Wild Islands
programme.desc: The Falkland Islands' pristine coastlines and bountiful seas offer a lifeline and breeding centre for millions of penguins each year. Though while some find sanctuary on dry land, there's a daily battle to survive in the waters which surround these wild and rocky shores.

programme.title: Coasts - Rolling with the Waves
programme.desc: We love our coasts, and so do animals! The corridor of water where the open ocean transitions into coastal habitat is known as the surf zone. The churning forces of the waves clashing with the land make these some of the most food-rich waters on Earth. Nutrients are both washed off the coast from rain and rivers, but also pushed up from the depths thanks to waves and currents.

programme.title: World of the Wild
programme.desc: Wildlife that inhabits mountainous regions has be able to survive successfully at high altitudes. Any creature that lives in the mountains must also be able to cope with changing temperatures. Many species of hoofed and herbivorous mammal such as GOATS, DEER, SHEEP AND LLAMAS have adapted well to living high in the mountains and are often found grazing on ledges and on cliff faces. These herbivores in turn attract large predators such as BEARS, COUGARS AND MOUNTAIN LIONS.

programme.title: Wildest Places: Australia
programme.desc: Wildest Places explores some of the most incredible natural habitats on earth & a diverse range of wildlife.

programme.title: Coasts - Life's a Beach
programme.desc: To us the beach is one giant playground, but for wildlife it's a place to live, to find food and to raise their young. Amongst the fish and chips, sandcastles and donkey rides it's easy to forget that beaches are vital habitats, home to a myriad of animals. Whether grey seals are duelling for a mate and raising their young, or black bears and tigers are scouring the coastline for a tasty snack, animals have been using the beach for millennia.

programme.title: Naledi: A Baby Elephant's Tale
programme.desc: Under a blanket of stars on an African night, in the serene grasslands of Botswana's Okavango Delta, something rarely witnessed by humankind is about to happen: the much-anticipated birth of a baby elephant. An emotional life-or-death drama that champions the struggle of Africa's native elephant population, Naledi: A Baby Elephant's Tale tells the urgent story of an international crisis.

programme.title: Wild and Alive
programme.desc: On the coast of south Africa, a group of mammoth mammals is arriving from the deep ocean. Every year humpback and southern right whales make incredible migrations from the Antarctic seas to mate and give birth along southern Africa's rich protected coast. Just arriving in time won't be enough to guarantee a mate. Humpbacks conduct awe-inspiring aerial displays and chaotic competitions for attention before showing off their grace in underwater ballets.

programme.title: Deserts
programme.desc: All habitats present difficulties, but the challenges of the desert are more obvious than most - scorching heat and a lack food and water make them one of the most hostile environments on the planet. But with great challenges come incredible solutions. Despite the deadly conditions, a hardy band of unique animal and plant species have adapted to meet the inhospitable desert conditions head on.

programme.title: Hannah Goes to Namibia
programme.desc: Hannah Emde meets one of Africa's most experienced elephant trackers: Hendrick Munembome, the Director of Elephant Human Relations Aid (EHRA). The struggle for water often makes elephants and humans rivals in Namibia. Therefore, EHRA builds water wells for the elephants with volunteers from all over the world, far away from the villages. Hannah helps dig a ditch for a pipeline, then heads up the dry Ugab riverbed in search of the endangered Mama Afrika' herd.

programme.title: Cost of Progress
programme.desc: The natural world is in crisis. For years humanity has exploited the planet's resources, and the creatures that live here. Growth and innovation can be a marvelous thing, but at what cost to our one and only planet? When we continue to push ahead blindly, it's more often than not Mother Nature that pays the price. Now it is time for us to rally - to take heed and start to turn back the tide. It's time for us to recognize our part in this crisis and redress the balance of the cost of progress.

programme.title: British Garden: Life And Death On Your Lawn
programme.desc: The British back garden is a familiar setting, but underneath the peonies and petunias is a much wilder hidden world, a miniature Serengeti, with beauty and brutality in equal measure. In this 90-minute documentary Chris Packham and a team of wildlife experts spend an entire year exploring every inch of a series of interlinked back gardens in Welwyn Garden City. They want to answer a fundamental question: how much wildlife lives beyond our back doors?

programme.title: Fight for Life
programme.desc: Nature is red in tooth and claw - animals face daily battles to protect themselves and secure the resources they need to survive. Every battle is a trade-off between energy spent, the risk to health and the prizes awarded to the victors. Each fighter has a unique set of tools and techniques available to dispatch their opponents. For predators to find food, lower links in the food chain have a fight on their hands escaping the jaws of death. Their only options are to die, run or turn and fight.

programme.title: Destination Wild - Wild Argentina
programme.desc: This episode follows the animals of Argentina, living life at the mercy of the Andean mountains. These peaks dictate a hard existence for every living creature from their summits to the very edge of the Patagonian steppe, forcing even the cutest resident to turn carnivore... Predators stalk the foothills and creepy crawlies lie low in the sandy steppe. Every animal here has a bloodthirsty drive to survive.

programme.title: Lion - Africa's Super Power
programme.desc: The endless plains of East Africa is a paradise for lions. The most social of all cats, lions form prides that are unlike any other animals. Together, they'll hunt, raise their young and defend their territory. With such a close family and plentiful home, the pride welcomes new babies every year. But new children introduces new dangers.

programme.title: January (Nature's Calendar)
programme.desc: In Europe in January, we sit around in the dark, missing the bright lights and festivities of Christmas, perhaps it would cheer us up to imagine January around the world. To the north, polar bear cubs are born and nestle against their hibernating mothers, but on the other side of the planet, kangaroos are experiencing the highest temperatures and having to trek in search of water, while in East Africa, wildebeest arrive on their breeding grounds and enjoy a baby-boom on a giant scale.

programme.title: Wild and Alive
programme.desc: In the heart of the Ivory Coast a small rural village has a very special resident. The last white rhino in the country sleeps on the village outskirts and feeds on the villagers' crops. He's survived a gunshot to the shoulder and a decade of civil war, and he's something of a celebrity here. But all is not well. The rhino has killed the chief of the village, and it's time for him to go.

programme.title: Magical Fjords
programme.desc: Fjords are one of the most dramatic landscapes on Earth, but their majesty is just the tip of the iceberg. Fjords stand witness to some of the greatest wonders of the animal kingdom. Fjords are found in a frozen land where only the toughest survive. Whether just below the surface, at the murky depths of the sea floor or on dry land, the fjords offer an incredible bounty to wildlife.

programme.title: Destination Wild - Wild Islands
programme.desc: Nestled alongside Canada's south west coast, Vancouver Island is home to the richest Pacific wildlife. Sea lions and killer whales are among the marine predators enjoying the abundant seafood in the surrounding waters, while black bears, marmots and beavers enjoy the rich pickings on land. But each fall, the islands inhabitants must adapt and prepare to face the coming winter. Some will leave, among them humpback whales and turkey vultures who migrate to warmer climes.

programme.title: Fighting for a Mate
programme.desc: Animals face daily battles to protect themselves and secure the resources they need to survive. Every battle is a trade-off between the risk to health and the prizes awarded to the victors. Each animal fights with a unique set of tools, from display structures and elaborate body language to claws, jaws and antlers. And few fights are as fuelled as those during breeding season; the ultimate trophy for the brave fighter is, of course, a chance to pass on the fighting genes to the next generation.

programme.title: Animals of Thanksgiving
programme.desc: Thanksgiving. A most treasured holiday, and not just in the USA; it continues to be celebrated across the world in many different guises. These traditions are all united by a celebration of the harvest and the generosity of the natural world. Many animals have weird and wonderful connections to the holidays. Turkeys are one of the most iconic characters, but deer, lobsters and even eagles are also part of the feast.

programme.title: World's Wildest City: Anchorage
programme.desc: When Spring comes one animal arrives in its thousands. It's the salmon. Travelling an incredible 3500 miles through rivers and streams they are Alaska's hardiest resident. Using their muscular bodies they can swim up stream jumping over any obstacle that comes in their way. But there is one grizzly hazard they face right at the end of their journey. It's the brown bears. These expert fishermen use skill and accuracy to grab onto the salmon with their powerful teeth.

programme.title: The Miracle Of The Cards
programme.desc: There's no such thing as miracles. That's what a skeptical reporter (Kirk Cameron) thought until he met Craig Shergold (Thomas Sangster). Craig is an eight-year-old boy with a brain tumor and less than a year to live. Looking for hope, his mother (Catherine Oxenberg) pushes to break the Guinness World Record for receiving the most get-well cards. They receive an incredible 1.3 million cards and shatter the old record. However Craig continues to get worse.

programme.desc: "Hank's Christmas Wish" tells the heartwarming tale of a retired elf seeking a life of seclusion. However, his plans are interrupted when a group of unrelentingly cheerful townsfolk, brimming with the holiday spirit, come into his life. Through their unwavering kindness and infectious joy, they help him rediscover the true meaning of Christmas. Packed with yuletide laughter, chestnut-roasting moments, and Jack Frost-nipping faith, this cutesy film captures the essence of the holiday season.

programme.title: The Messenger's Box
programme.desc: When high school student Jake Casper finds a small wooden box in the attic of his grandpa's antique store, his life is forever changed, especially when he discovers a secret compartment that appears to contain a nail used during Christ's crucifixion. Now, the more Jake learns of the power within the box and its purpose, the more obstacles he must overcome to get the box to a stranger before it's too late.

programme.desc: Singer Donna Summer died from cancer on May 17, 2012, with the public having no idea she was ill.

programme.title: Crimes Uncovered
programme.desc: The story of Cezanne Visser, her partner Dirk Prinsloo and how they callously broke the law and left a trail of broken lives in their wake.
programme.sub-title: Sordid Lies: The Cezanne Visser Story

programme.title: World's Most Evil Killers
programme.desc: It is widely believed that Tobin is the 1960s Scottish serial killer known as Bible John.

programme.title: Takedown with Chris Hansen
programme.desc: Over the past two decades, Chris Hansen's investigations have led to hundreds of would-be sex criminals being stopped in their tracks. Amazingly, after 500 arrests and hundreds of millions of video views, men continue to try to meet children online. So, his mission continues.

programme.title: Child Snatchers
programme.desc: Belinda's efforts to go to Turkey in search of Cihan are delayed; Andreas fights to get his daughter back from Poland.

programme.title: True Crime Nation with Chris Hansen
programme.desc: Host Chris Hansen and our talented team of veteran crime producers bring you a closer look at the crimes affecting our nation.

programme.title: Becoming Evil: Cult of Personality
programme.desc: Killers Without Conscience - H.H.Holmes and Jane Toppan. The phenomenon of serial killing moved to America late in the 19th century with two of the country's most brutal killers - Chicago's Dr. Death, H.H. Holmes, and a Boston nurse, Jane Toppan.
programme.sub-title: Killers Without Conscience - H.H.Holmes and Jane Toppan

programme.title: Crime Time Solvers
programme.desc: A day before her 18th birthday, the body of Marie Varnerot, a 17-year-old girl, was found half-naked on her bed in Maincy, near Melun.
programme.sub-title: Murdered on the Eve of Adulthood

programme.title: Blood, Lies And Alibis
programme.desc: Mr. Hopkins, a preacher in Alabama, has the perfect family until his wife disappears. Secrets then come forward in a story of horror and perversion.

programme.title: Court Martial: Soldiers Behind Bars
programme.desc: Staff bring out the dogs, turning the place upside down, hunting for a forbidden mobile.

programme.title: Murder Maps
programme.desc: At the time of Jack The Ripper, London was home to some of the most terrible individuals the city has ever seen.

programme.title: Mind Investigators
programme.desc: In June 2011, a man is arrested for brutal domestic homicide. This horrible story is the story of a sadistic pulsion.

programme.title: The Interrogation Room Hosted by Vivica A. Fox
programme.desc: Lee Rodarte Jr., a chef at Bonefish Grill in Jacksonville, Florida, murdered his colleague and ex-lover Savannah Gold.

programme.title: Crimes Uncovered
programme.desc: On the eve of her 21st birthday, Leigh Matthews is kidnapped from her college campus and held for ransom by an unknown assailant.
programme.sub-title: A Family's Nightmare Begins: The Leigh Matthews Story Part 1

programme.title: Becoming Evil: Secret Language of Serial Killers
programme.desc: Uncover the dark side of advertising. From Jack the Ripper to the Son of Sam, serial killers have utilized branding, ad space, and other methods in chilling combinations to make themselves famous.

programme.title: Caught on Bodycam
programme.desc: Raw bodycam footage capturing high-stake police incidents.

programme.title: Caught on Bodycam
programme.desc: Raw bodycam footage capturing high-stake police incidents.

programme.title: Nurses Who Kill
programme.desc: Nurse Roger Dean said he loved the residents at the care home where he worked just outside Sydney, Australia, but loved the drugs he was addicted to more. Unfortunately, he strongly suspected that he had been caught on camera stealing them. He set the place on fire and killed 10 people. Mark Tedeschi reveals the evidence he took to court to win a conviction against Nurse Dean.

programme.title: Nurses Who Kill
programme.desc: Jeannie M Miata aka Jeanine Hannah is serving life in a prison for murdering a 68-year-old Texas woman with a lethal dose of insulin and for the suspicious death of 78-year-old Anne Jones. Inside prison, Emmy Award-winning journalist Carolyn Canville went head-to-head with a serial-killer nurse who, in the face of over-whelming evidence to the contrary, still protests her innocence.

programme.title: Under Arrest
programme.desc: An illegal drinking establishment is raided, a taxi driver is assaulted and a K-9 unit tracks a car thief.

programme.title: Under Arrest
programme.desc: Police attend a bloody attempted suicide, an impaired driver with two wives and burglars are apprehended.

programme.title: Crimes That Made History
programme.desc: In 1888, a series of gruesome murders shocked London: The perpetrator was dubbed "Jack the Ripper". This was the Victorian era, when puritanism reigned and forensic science was in its infancy. How did these factors combine to create one of the most renowned crime stories in history, resulting in the construction of the serial killer?

programme.title: Crimes That Made History
programme.desc: Paris, January 1907. Albert Soleilland is accused of the rape and murder of a little girl - Marthe. The press details every step of the case as if it was a show. As early century France was on the verge of abolishing the death sentence, that infamous crime set the abolitionist cause back decades - the media massively and eagerly asked for his execution.
programme.sub-title: Albert Soleilland: A Case for the Death Penalty (1907)

programme.title: Killer Mysteries
programme.desc: When three members of the same family die of mysterious causes, police suspect foul play.

programme.title: Killer Mysteries
programme.desc: When a newly married woman is killed at home, police believe it's a robbery gone wrong.

programme.title: Deadly Standoffs
programme.desc: Randy and Vicki Weaver were involved in an 11-day siege after retreating to the mountainside of Ruby Ridge; re-examining the deadly 1992 standoff which left two dead.

programme.title: Forensics
programme.desc: A handless body is washed up on the shores of a wild wellington beach in mid-winter. Identification of this mutilated corpse is the first challenge for investigators. Someone has gone to a lot of trouble to mask the identity of the victim.

programme.title: Bloodline Detectives hosted by Nancy Grace
programme.desc: In Sacramento, three women are assaulted by the same man. Police use genealogy technology to find the suspect.

programme.title: Women Behind Bars
programme.desc: A man who had molested his daughter for a number of years is shot and killed by his daughter. Next, a murder witness is tortured and murdered by a gang member.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: When a 35-year-old woman dies in her sleep, the hospital is unable to find a cause of death; Dr. G tries to provide some answers for her devastated family.

programme.title: Gangsters: America's Most Evil
programme.desc: Giancana is connected to conspiracy theories involving both the Kennedy family and Fidel Castro.

programme.title: Casualty 24/7
programme.desc: Staffing problems hit the ER as nurses call in sick and the team is forced to juggle extra patients. A family in a road traffic accident is admitted with possible damage to the driver's spine.

programme.title: True Crime Nation with Chris Hansen
programme.desc: Host Chris Hansen and our talented team of veteran crime producers bring you a closer look at the crimes affecting our nation.

programme.title: Becoming Evil: Cult of Personality
programme.desc: The Bogeyman's Gonna Eat You - Albert Fish, the Vampire of Brooklyn. Program 3 examines the demented life of Albert Fish, who earned his ghoulish nickname, the Vampire of Brooklyn, by preying on America's most innocent - children
programme.sub-title: The Bogeyman's Gonna Eat You - Albert Fish, the Vampire of Brooklyn

programme.title: Crime Time Solvers
programme.desc: In Saint-Andéol-Le-Château, Rhône, the Lyon Research Brigade investigates a quadruple homicide where an entire family was killed with the same weapon.

programme.title: The Lady Killers
programme.desc: A love triangle between two sisters and one of their husbands led to a shocking murder. Detectives look back at the case that proved love can ruin any family bond.

programme.title: Crimes of Passion
programme.desc: A financier lives after his socialite wife shoots him six times in their Calgary condo.

programme.title: Court Martial: Soldiers Behind Bars
programme.desc: A detainee guilty of indecent misconduct fights for his freedom.

programme.title: The Lonesome Dove Collection
programme.desc: A series of disasters overtakes Colonel Cobb and his ambition to annex Sante Fe including dust storms, prairie fires, Indians, and the Mexican army.
programme.sub-title: Larry McMurtry's Dead Man's Walk, Pt. 2

programme.title: The Lonesome Dove Collection
programme.desc: After surrendering to the Mexican army, the expedition's captors march them across 500 miles of desert to New Mexico.
programme.sub-title: Larry McMurtry's Dead Man's Walk, Pt. 3

programme.title: An Eye for an Eye
programme.desc: Ex-bounty hunter Talion (Robert Lansing) comes home one day to find his house ablaze and his entire family slaughtered. He soon learns that the culprits are a gang led by nasty Ike Slant (Slim Pickens). While tracking the outlaws, Talion meets fellow bounty hunter Benny (Pat Wayne), who's also after Ike. Initially mistrustful of each another, Benny and Talion are forced to work together when, during a shootout with the criminals, the latter is blinded and the former injures his shooting hand.

programme.title: One-Eyed Jacks
programme.desc: After pulling a bank heist in Mexico, the outlaw Rio (Marlon Brando) and his partner, Dad Longworth (Karl Malden), make a run for it, but Dad has bigger plans than freedom. He betrays Rio and absconds with the loot, and Rio ends up in prison. Years pass before Rio finally breaks free to enact his long-plotted revenge. Tracking Dad to California, Rio learns he's become a sheriff -- which is no deterrent -- but when Rio falls for Dad's stepdaughter, Louisa (Pina Pellicer), he has second thoughts.

programme.title: Blindspots
programme.desc: James and his older brother Colton head to Austin, Texas to sample BBQ from a blind pitmaster and live music from a blind musician; ashort road trip to Houston connects them with blind celebrity chef Christine Ha.

programme.title: Blindspots
programme.desc: James and his sister Cassie visit Frankfurt and Mainz, enjoying beer and brats, and exploring Germany's infrastructure of support for the visually impaired; this culminates in a tour of the Dialogue Museum.

programme.title: Blindspots
programme.desc: James and his sister Cassie travel to Zurich and visit ETH Zurich, the MIT of Europe, where they try out prototypes of new technological solutions for accessibility; they venture to the top of a tall peak in Davos for an evening in an igloo.

programme.title: Blindspots
programme.desc: In Tokyo, a city of over 24 million, James tries not to get lost in the crowd as he attempts to conquer his fear of seafood, meets a blind breakdancer, and learns how the sighted and blind alike prepare for the city's next natural disaster.

programme.title: Blindspots
programme.desc: The bullet train takes James to Osaka and toward his ultimate goal: to climb Mount Fuji; outside the big cities, James searches for peace in Kyoto's temples; sacred traditions and a mountain covered in monkeys offer a new perspective on life.

programme.title: Blindspots
programme.desc: James returns to his former home city of Los Angeles, where he reconnects with old friends working in accessibility in the entertainment industry, enjoys Korean BBQ, street food, and hits the beach for a little surfing.

programme.title: Blindspots
programme.desc: After a surprise invite to visit the head of accessibility at Microsoft's headquarters in Seattle, James heads to Vancouver, known for its breathtaking natural beauty and self-proclaimed title of "most accessible city in the world."

programme.title: Blindspots
programme.desc: James sets out to discover what it's like to travel blind in the Big Apple, to see if someone like him can make it there.

programme.title: Blindspots
programme.desc: James heads across the pond to discover what life for a blind traveler is like in a world capital like London; he dives into the nation's crown cuisine of Indian food and learns a new sport, created by and for the visually impaired.

programme.title: Butterfly Effect
programme.desc: Early in their history, humans realize that they can affect nature by controlling fire, making tools and taming wild animals; what they were not given by nature, they harnessed in other species.

programme.title: Butterfly Effect
programme.desc: From the mysterious megaliths in prehistory to the first hot air balloons and the construction of the Giza pyramid complex, ancestors have always observed and experimented to gain a better understanding of their world.
programme.sub-title: Gravity: It All Falls Into Place!

programme.title: Butterfly Effect
programme.desc: A journey through the key events that have allowed people to better understand the world of microbe.
programme.sub-title: Viruses and Bacteria: Tiny but Tough

programme.title: Butterfly Effect
programme.desc: A journey through the key moments that enabled humanity to discover plastics.

programme.title: Butterfly Effect
programme.desc: Long-distance communication, moving stealthily through the dark without being detected, and observation from afar have all become commonplace; at any moment, one can know exactly where one is on the planet.

programme.title: Butterfly Effect
programme.desc: The understanding of energy enables people to send rockets into space; learning what exactly is energy and where it comes from.

programme.title: Butterfly Effect
programme.desc: Running climate simulations on a global scale; learning to control rivers and protect against flooding.
programme.sub-title: Fluid Mechanics: A Source of Inspiration

programme.title: Butterfly Effect
programme.desc: The development of incredible technologies, from the infinitely small to the infinitely large; a journey through the key moments that allow humanity to discover quantum physics.
programme.sub-title: Quantum Physics: A Step Into Unknown

programme.title: Butterfly Effect
programme.desc: Many natural phenomena are based on the laws of physics; forecasting the weather several days in advance; asking if it is possible to predict everything.
programme.sub-title: Chaos Theory: Small Causes, Great Effects

programme.title: Butterfly Effect
programme.desc: Countless machines are used to perform hard work in one's daily life, with each of them obeying a specific program custom-written in a particular language.

programme.title: Butterfly Effect
programme.desc: Handling numbers so large that all the books in the world would not be enough to contain them; societies are profoundly reliant on an increasingly complex equation.
programme.sub-title: Mathematics: How to Speak to Robots?

programme.title: Butterfly Effect
programme.desc: People just begin to understand what happens beneath their feet in the heart of the planet, to be better equipped to predict and prepare for tomorrow's volcanic eruptions or tsunamis.

programme.title: Destruction Decoded
programme.desc: When water unleashes its rage upon the planet, it becomes the ultimate bringer of death; whether it's from rain washing over the ground, rivers bursting their banks, or failed efforts to stem the flow, flooding is as inevitable as it is unstoppable.

programme.title: Destruction Decoded
programme.desc: Bridges and tunnels revolutionized transportation-but when they fail, tragedy follows. This episode explores the world's worst collapses and fires, including a tunnel blaze in the Alps so intense it fused 20 cars together. While bridge failures send vehicles plummeting into water or ground below, tunnel fires turn confined spaces into infernos. Why do these disasters happen, and what can be done to stop them? As we build bigger and faster, we also raise the stakes.

programme.title: Destruction Decoded

programme.title: Destruction Decoded

programme.desc: Hurricanes, typhoons and cyclones are all the same thing with different names, but what they also have in common is their destructive power.

programme.title: Destruction Decoded
programme.desc: Earthquakes occur when tectonic plates suddenly shift and shock waves shake the Earth's surface; they occur along fault lines -- the most active being the Ring of Fire in the Pacific Ocean and the San Andreas Fault on the American West Coast.

programme.title: Destruction Decoded
programme.desc: Volcanoes created more than 80% of our planet's surface, but explosive eruptions can be deadly; a journey under the earth to discover why volcanoes are so dangerous.

programme.title: Destruction Decoded
programme.desc: Tornadoes are violent, rotating columns of air that can level buildings, their unpredictability makes them even more destructive; a look at how tornadoes form and if they can be stopped.

programme.title: Destruction Decoded
programme.desc: When water unleashes its rage upon the planet, it becomes the ultimate bringer of death; whether it's from rain washing over the ground, rivers bursting their banks, or failed efforts to stem the flow, flooding is as inevitable as it is unstoppable.

programme.title: Butterfly Effect
programme.desc: People just begin to understand what happens beneath their feet in the heart of the planet, to be better equipped to predict and prepare for tomorrow's volcanic eruptions or tsunamis.

programme.title: Travels with Darley
programme.desc: Join Darley on a revolutionary road trip in South Carolina. Historic sites and untold stories speak to the American Revolution, including visits to The Charleston Museum, Heyward Washington House, and restaurants with Gullah Geechee roots.
programme.sub-title: South Carolina: Revolutionary Road Trip - Part 1

programme.title: Travels with Darley
programme.desc: Darley's revolutionary road trip continues in New Jersey. Visit the State Archives and view original documents related to America's founding, and become familiar with authentic period dress and untold stories of the American Revolution.
programme.sub-title: New Jersey: Revolutionary Road Trip - Part 1

programme.title: Travels with Darley
programme.desc: Our revolutionary road trip in New Jersey with Darley continues as we immerse ourselves in colonial times through interactive history with local experts and follow in George Washington's footsteps. This is where history takes center stage.
programme.sub-title: New Jersey: Revolutionary Road Trip - Part 2

programme.title: Travels with Darley
programme.desc: The final leg of our revolutionary road trip in New Jersey includes a visit to Morristown National Historical Park and a tour of Perth Amboy's Propriety House. Darley also takes us to East Jersey Old Town to examine historic structures.
programme.sub-title: New Jersey: Revolutionary Road Trip - Part 3

programme.title: Tom Kerridge's Proper Pub Food
programme.desc: Cooking for friends should not be time-consuming and should be a big hit with your friends. So, how do you accomplish this? Think: Sunday roast and a slow cooker, or mussels in ale. What about a hearty chorizo and chickpea stew?

programme.title: Tom Kerridge's Proper Pub Food
programme.desc: We all enjoy eating outdoors in a beer garden, and Tom wants to show us how to create outdoor food properly. Chicken in a basket with a twist, a tasty fish burger, a delicious maple cake, extra special barbecued beef ribs... it is chow time.

programme.title: Tom Kerridge's Proper Pub Food
programme.desc: Tom prepares decadent, showstopping dishes for special occasions, including an elegant asparagus served with his ultimate salad dressing, a slow-roast duck, deep-fried oysters, spiced monkfish, and a refreshing gin and tonic granita.

programme.title: Steven Raichlen's Project Smoke
programme.desc: Get an inside look at the tools and fuels for creative ribs! Make gigantic beef ribs, jerk spareribs smoked over pimento wood, and spice-smoked lamb ribs with cherry BBQ sauce. Plus, try apple-hickory coleslaw and bacon-cheddar cornbread.

programme.title: Steven Raichlen's Project Fire
programme.desc: Steak through the ages has been the ultimate symbol of luxury. If you crave embellishment, it's the perfect foil for all the rubs, marinades, butters, and sauces. It's easy to grill, but you can spend a lifetime seeking perfection.

programme.title: Tastes Like Home
programme.desc: Thanks to a lesson on behalf of Marie's father, Catherine, now armed with a traditional family recipe for a Swedish smorgasbord, now must travel to the Gap of Dunloe and attempt to recreate the smorgasbord for Marie's family and friends.

programme.title: Tastes Like Home
programme.desc: Catherine fondly recalls the generosity she experienced throughout her travels before she sets off to soak in Spain's amazing culinary world. Catherine also prepares and shares a few of her favorite Spanish dishes in the kitchen.

programme.title: Steven Raichlen's Project Smoke
programme.desc: It's surf and turf on Project Smoke! Smoke up this classic combo with chipotle shrimp cocktail, cedar-planked bacon-wrapped trout, reverse-seared Santa Maria tri-tip, and Chinese tea-smoked duck tacos.

programme.title: Andiamo! Uptown
programme.desc: In the second part of her tour of Alberta, Canada, you and Donna will discover fresh cuisine at the local farmer's market and explore some of the region's crafts. You will also go snowshoeing and learn how to ski.

programme.title: Taste Hunters
programme.desc: Mont Saint-Michel Bay in France is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located between Brittany and Lower Normandy. This marvel of the Western world is encapsulated within a vast bay where some of the largest tides in Europe can be experienced.

programme.title: Traveling with Denella Ri'chard
programme.desc: The subtropical climate of the U.S. Virgin Islands makes for an ideal year-round destination. Add soft-powder sand beaches, delicious Caribbean cooking, and stunning islands views, and it becomes clear that here, you will revive your soul.

programme.title: What's Eating Harlem
programme.desc: Enriching the community is the goal of Clay N.Y.C., shine a spotlight on the female African American body as depicted throughout history, experience the Harlem Arts Festival, and behold the collaborative environment of WeWork.

programme.title: Culinary Travels With Dave Eckert
programme.desc: Get ready to explore the wonders of Single Malt Whisky with Culinary Travels. We will tour the famous Glenfiddich Distillery before taste testing an amazing glass of Balvenie.

programme.title: What's Eating Harlem
programme.desc: Raphael Benavides Baccus speaks with us about his two legendary establishments: The Cecil Steakhouse and Minton's Playhouse, Film Producer Nadhege Ptah sheds light on the film "Paris Blues in Harlem," and we learn how Harlem fights cancer.

programme.title: Steven Raichlen's Project Fire
programme.desc: From California to Korea, Japan, and Southeast Asia, grilled meats with herbs, spices, chilies, and soy sauce meet healthy vegetables, barbecue as health food. Steven visits Jenee Kim for grilled beef short ribs.

programme.title: Andiamo! Uptown
programme.desc: Travel to Zurich, Switzerland, Europe's undisputed capital of finance, where you and Donna will enjoy the city's history, culture, cuisine, and high-end shopping in what is an extremely clean and cosmopolitan city.

programme.title: Steven Raichlen's Project Fire
programme.desc: One Good Turn: Rotisserie grilling combines smoky sear with roasting heat. Benefits include basting, no flare-ups, and wood smoke fragrance. Game hens with crispy skin, huli-huli spare ribs, glazed wings, and a sugar-crusted spinning pineapple finish the feast.

programme.title: Taste Hunters
programme.desc: Sicily is an island steeped in history, culture, and agricultural production. Since antiquity, Sicily's inhabitants have mastered the exceptional resources of their land, including its rich soil that has benefited from volcanic curing.

programme.title: Culinary Travels With Dave Eckert
programme.desc: We are "going gourmet" in paradise with Culinary Travels in Puerto Vallarta, Mexico. Prior to finding out what some of the truly amazing top local chefs are cooking, we begin with taste testing some tequila.

programme.title: The Toque 12
programme.desc: Phil's first stop on our Malaysian culinary tour is Aliyaa Island Restaurant where Chef Pradeep Kumar shares some of his tasteful preparations and cooking secrets and takes us shopping for fresh spices and ingredients.

programme.title: Steven Raichlen's Project Smoke
programme.desc: Explore a region you don't normally associate with smoking: Asia. From Chinese char siu pork to smoky tangerine flan, learn to create a unique fusion of Asian barbecue and American wood smoke.

programme.title: Tastes Like Home
programme.desc: His love of horses provided Peter with the impetus to live on Jeju Island, South Korea. With a desire to send Peter a taste from home, his wife Grainne teaches Catherine how to make his favorite dish of roast stuffed fillet of pork.

programme.title: Mexico: One Plate at a Time with Rick Bayless
programme.desc: Ever travel to a tourist mecca and wonder what the locals eat? Join Rick and his friend Hugo to find the best Mexican food in Los Cabos. First stop is the municipal market in San Jose del Cabo, then they enjoy carnitas at Los Michoacános.
programme.sub-title: Eat Like a Local in Los Cabos

programme.title: What's Eating Harlem
programme.desc: Joey Harris's impressive music portfolio defies belief, while Stacey Toussaint paints a vivid picture of how slavery infected historical America.

programme.title: Steven Raichlen's Project Fire
programme.desc: Gators fans and sports lovers of all persuasions get pumped for tailgate parties because good barbecue makes the perfect prelude to the game. Steve shows how his home state of Florida re-imagines three tailgate classics.

programme.title: The Toque 12
programme.desc: Jaan by Kirk Westaway has ranked among the highest rated Singaporean restaurants for some time now, and Chef Julien Royer is a major reason for their success. Follow Phil into Chef Royer's kitchen to experience the master at work.

programme.title: Traveling with Denella Ri'chard
programme.desc: When Denella thinks of Jamaica she cannot help but smile, for it is in here where she does not have to worry about a thing, because everything is 'irie.' Heavenly sunrises, magnificent sunsets, visit Jamaica and become one with nature.

programme.title: The Toque 12
programme.desc: An homage to the good things in life, Ku De Ta is a Bali icon known for its soulful sophistication and is an establishment Phillip Davenport knows intimately. Executive Chef Ben Cross prepares some of Ku De Ta's premier signature dishes.

programme.title: Steven Raichlen's Project Fire
programme.desc: Steven shares So-Cal grilling classics like fish tacos reimagined with wood fire, Caribbean-style char-grilled lobsters with orange mojo. Chef Anthony Endy updates South American chimichurri. Bold California flavors meet fire and smoke.

programme.title: Steven Raichlen's Project Smoke
programme.desc: Once you get the hang of smoking, you can smoke just about everything. Discover how to use electric smokers, pellet grills, ceramic cookers, and stovetop kettle smokers to add soulful smoke flavors to a four-course meal.

programme.title: Ottolenghi's Mediterranean Feast
programme.desc: Turkish cuisine channels cultural currents from all compass points, and Istanbul is the perfect city to experience this cornucopia of unique culinary dishes. Ottolenghi also dines at Asitane Restaurant, visits the Grand Bazaar, and more.

programme.title: The Toque 12
programme.desc: With its own signature Marble 8 Cuts, Marble 8 Steakhouse redefines dry-aged beef, and as host Phillip Davenport soon discovers, this is the pinnacle of steakhouse dining. Chef Simone Musu features the surf and turf classics of Marble 8.

programme.title: Takeaway Titans
programme.desc: The winners of each round return to the kitchen for the chance of becoming Ireland's top Takeaway Titan, but to do so they must thoroughly impress Chef Dylan McGrath, takeaway expert Suzie Lee, and 25 hungry members of the public.

programme.title: Taste Hunters
programme.desc: Discover Cape Town and the surrounding region of South Africa where two oceans meet. Surrounded by the Table Mountain range, Cape Town enjoys a Mediterranean climate, fertile soil, and lush vineyards that exist beside overpopulated towns.

programme.title: The Healthy Voyager's Global Kitchen
programme.desc: Carolyn Scott-Hamilton, the Healthy Voyager, demonstrates how to prepare a Rum and Pumpkin Cocktail, Chocolate Cyclops Eyeballs, Pumpkin and Toffee Bread Pudding, and Caramel and Chocolate Popcorn, for the healthy vegan Halloweener in you.

programme.title: My Greek Table with Diane Kochilas
programme.desc: Experience the wonderful world of Greek cheeses. In Epirus, Diane follows feta cheese from its artisanal roots to modern production. We will also explore a range of other cheeses, visit a shepherd in Zagorohoria, and make farmhouse cheese.

programme.title: The Toque 12 - Master Chefs
programme.desc: Meet the genius behind Chef Nancy Silverton and witness her make one of her celebrated pizzas from scratch. Mario Batali provides sage advice for young chefs, and Wolfgang Puck and Greg Bess take you into their culinary world at Spago.

programme.title: Andiamo! Uptown
programme.desc: In Alberta, Canada, Donna's first impression is- snow. And she enjoys it to the fullest. Donna finds myriad ways of taking advantage of a snowy environment, including snow-biking, ice walking, and staying at a world-renowned resort.

programme.title: Steven Raichlen's Project Fire
programme.desc: Wine and barbecue have deep roots. In Santa Ynez, grapevines fuel fires, and wine is used in marinades. Dishes include Jidori chicken stuffed with ham & cheese, grilled flank steak with Pinot Noir sauce, and bourbon-soaked wagyu strip loin smoked by Chef John Cox.

programme.title: Tastes Like Home
programme.desc: Alexandra and her family moved to Ireland in the 1990s from Russia. After tasting some of their beloved family dishes, Catherine travels to Mexico where Alexandra's sister, Anna, introduces her to Mayan cooking and 5-star Mexican cuisine.

programme.title: Taste Hunters
programme.desc: Hong Kong is among the world's most interesting cities. Its name means "Fragrant Harbor." In modern times, many aspects of Hong Kong's culture come to mind before the topic of agriculture, however, sustainable production is here to stay.

programme.title: Mexico: One Plate at a Time with Rick Bayless
programme.desc: Join Rick and winemaker Hugo d'Acosta as they toast the world-class wines of Baja California Norte. Hugo first introduces Rick his Casa de Piedra wines before moving on to Tres Mujeres, L.A. Cetto, and the San Rafael Winery.

programme.title: Tastes Like Home
programme.desc: Catherine travels to Osijek where she soaks in the local culture before learning how to prepare Croatian Sarma, a dish the Matkovic family is hoping she will pass along to them so they may create and savor their own tastes from home.

programme.title: The Healthy Voyager's Global Kitchen
programme.desc: Carolyn Scott-Hamilton, the Healthy Voyager, demonstrates how to prepare Walnut Tacos, Enchiladas with Tomatillo Sauce, and Colombian Arepas, all of which will hit the mark with the healthy vegan voyager in you.

programme.title: What's Eating Harlem
programme.desc: We will also enjoy an intimate conversation with Singer and Songwriter Esnavi, and the resplendent Lana Turner regales us with the history of Harlem's trains.

programme.title: My Greek Table with Diane Kochilas
programme.desc: Diane reveals the vast variety and robust flavors of the festive meze tradition of small plates of vibrant food meant to be shared. In Volos, she meets up with a Meze meister, and pushes the limits of meze at a cutting-edge restaurant.

programme.title: Traveling with Denella Ri'chard
programme.desc: Denella discovers there is more than just world-changing history in Montgomery. Not only does she stand in the footsteps of heroes like Rosa Parks and Dr. King, but she also finds outdoor adventure, world-class arts, and the heart and soul of the South.

programme.title: My Greek Table with Diane Kochilas
programme.desc: On a cruise to Mykonos, Diane discovers the quiet culture of its local farmers, not the dazzling side of Greece's party island. Join her as she cooks with a young chef who is breathing new life into the island's traditional recipes.

programme.title: My Greek Table with Diane Kochilas
programme.desc: Lesvos is among the most vibrant and fascinating Greek islands, where the crossroads of history is exemplified by local dishes featuring the sea's bounty, eggplant, and Ouzo. Diane gets an insider's taste with a good friend and local son.

programme.title: Steven Raichlen's Project Smoke
programme.desc: Learn to make bacon from scratch, plus a twist on Canadian bacon-pork loin smoked in fennel brine. Then, try the "Tulsa Torpedo," a 3-pound bacon-wrapped delight, and bacon-wrapped Snow Crab Poppers for a bacon surf and turf!

programme.title: The Toque 12
programme.desc: Inside The Westin in Kuala Lumpur, Phillip visits Prego where Executive Chef Aizat Hakim Feisal creates his impressive signature dishes. Phil also experiences QBA, an energetic bar that will take you back half a century to Havana, Cuba.

programme.title: The Toque 12
programme.desc: Malaysia's extraordinary restaurants can be found in the most amazing locations, and Phillip Davenport takes us to the best of them. Dato' Steve Day nurtured the country's progress towards culinary excellence, and here, we taste Malaysia.

programme.title: Steven Raichlen's Project Smoke
programme.desc: Make gourmet treats like mesquite-smoked oysters with chipotle BBQ sauce, 7-bone prime rib smoked on a rotisserie and seared over oak, triple-smoked potatoes with bacon and cheddar, and smoked cheesecake with burnt sugar cream sauce.

programme.title: Primal Grill with Steven Raichlen
programme.desc: In barbecue, bigger is often better-especially with beef. Every grill master should master big cuts like brisket, prime rib, and whole beef tenderloin. These showstoppers will impress your guests. Are you ready for the challenge?

programme.title: Traveling with Denella Ri'chard
programme.desc: Accompany Denella as she unveils the tranquil Caribbean vibes of St. John and St. Croix. Each island has dedicated much land to natural and historical preservation, and Denella meets the people who add their time and energy to that effort.

programme.title: The Healthy Voyager's Global Kitchen
programme.desc: Carolyn Scott-Hamilton, the Healthy Voyager, demonstrates how to prepare Dill Potato Pancakes, an Ackee Breakfast Scramble, Breakfast Quinoa, and a Spinach and Artichoke Bruschetta that are sure to satisfy the healthy vegan voyager in you.

programme.title: My Greek Table with Diane Kochilas

programme.title: Secrets of the Nazis
programme.desc: Amateur filmmakers in Normandy secretly documented daily life between 1939-1945, risking arrest under Nazi rule. Preserved for decades, their footage reveals war's darkest hours-shortages, fear, and ruins-yet also family bonds, joy, and hope. This documentary offers an extraordinary civilian perspective, intertwining anonymous lives with the unfolding tragedy and liberation of WWII.

programme.title: WWII: On the Edge of the Abyss
programme.desc: This episode takes viewers to 1945, a year filled with crucial events that shape the end of the war. The Yalta Conference, where Allied leaders discuss the post-war world, coincides with the final assaults on Germany. As Berlin falls and Hitler commits suicide, the Nazi regime finally collapses. The war in Europe is over, but the fight in the Pacific rages on.

programme.title: Battlezone WWII: Battle of Midway to Victory in the Pacific
programme.desc: A Japanese Corporal from the Tank Corps and a Sergeant from the US Army recollect the Liberation of the Philippines in 1944.

programme.title: Battlezone WWII: Battle of Midway to Victory in the Pacific
programme.desc: The liberation of Guam in 1944 from two and a half years of Japanese occupation.

programme.title: Battlezone WWII: Battle of Midway to Victory in the Pacific
programme.desc: The battle for the islands of Tarawa as told by a Japanese Sailor and a Sergeant for the US Marines.

programme.title: Battlezone WWII: Battle of Midway to Victory in the Pacific
programme.desc: A Japanese Infantryman and a US Marine Sergeant tell the story of their part in the US attack on the island of Iwo Jima.

programme.title: Battlezone WWII: Battle of Midway to Victory in the Pacific
programme.desc: A Japanese Airman and an American Seaman recount their memories of the attack on Okinawa and the role of the Kamikaze pilots.

programme.title: Battlezone WWII: Battle of Midway to Victory in the Pacific
programme.desc: A Japanese Fighter Pilot and an American airman remember the bombing of Japan in 1945, culminating in the atomic bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

programme.title: D-Day: The Longest of Days
programme.desc: Gen. Eisenhower and his aides map the Normandy invasion. German pictures show the extent of their coastal defenses. Tanks, guns, locomotives, and other military equipment is massed on the English beaches. Troops practice loading operations. Landing craft is tested in the English Channel. Pictures of practice landing and airborne operations are used to dramatize the actual invasion on June 6, 1944.

programme.title: Battlezone WWII: Battle of Midway to Victory in the Pacific
programme.desc: A Japanese Airman and an American Seaman recount their memories of the attack on Okinawa and the role of the Kamikaze pilots.

programme.title: Battlezone WWII: Battle of Midway to Victory in the Pacific
programme.desc: A Japanese Fighter Pilot and an American airman remember the bombing of Japan in 1945, culminating in the atomic bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

programme.title: Battlezone WWII: Battle of Midway to Victory in the Pacific
programme.desc: The build up of the US Navy prior to its battle with Japan for supremacy in the Pacific.

programme.title: Battlezone WWII: Battle of Midway to Victory in the Pacific
programme.desc: A Japanese Lieutenant and a Philippine Corporal remember the invasion of the Philippines by the Japanese in WWII.

programme.title: Embedded 45' Shooting War in Germany
programme.desc: This first episode covers the last week of February to late March. When American troops started their final invasion of Nazi Germany in February 1945, U.S. Army cameramen were at their side. Over a thousand reels have been preserved; many of them untouched for decades. The cameramen covered many stories of victory and defeat, death and liberation. Faces of despair and joy, scenes of war and peace.

programme.title: Battlezone WWII: The Big Battles
programme.desc: The final chapter in the Pacific with the allies eventually wresting control from the Japanese and the bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.
programme.sub-title: The Battle of the Pacific: The Setting Sun

programme.title: Naval Warfare in World War II
programme.desc: This episode explores the battles between the Allies and Germans near the Arctic Circle, and the convoys battling past German-occupied Norway to Russia.

programme.title: The US Battle For Supremacy In The Pacific
programme.desc: In 1943 John Ford gave the great cinematographer Gregg Toland (Citizen Kane, The Grapes of Wrath) an opportunity to direct his first film. A veritable epic, framed by a debate between Walter Huston's Uncle Sam and Harry Davenport's Mr. C on the true nature of the Pacific paradise, Pearl Harbor.

programme.title: The Crusade in the Pacific
programme.desc: This episode examines the relations between the United States, the Philippines, and Japan prior to World War II. Then it focuses on the Japanese invasion of Luzon, the take-over of Manila, and the eventual attack and seizure of Corregidor.

programme.title: The Crusade in the Pacific
programme.desc: This chapter presents the events that led to America's entry into World War II after the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941. It also shows the early setbacks and losses suffered by the Allies in the Pacific Theater, such as the fall of Wake Island, Guam, the Philippines, Hong Kong, Malaya, and Indonesia.
programme.sub-title: America Goes to War in the Pacific

programme.title: Battlezone WWII: The Gustav and Gothic Lines- Battle for Italy
programme.desc: Filmed entirely in Color, this documentary features Incredible air combat and ground attack attack action of a US Army Air Forces P-47 Thunderbolt group operating in Italy during 1944.

programme.title: WWII: On the Edge of the Abyss
programme.desc: The war reaches new levels of intensity as it drags on, affecting civilian populations like never before. The concept of 'total war' becomes reality, with cities bombed into oblivion, resources stretched to their limits, and entire societies mobilized for the war effort. Strategic bombing campaigns against Germany and Japan begin to devastate industrial centers and civilian morale alike.

programme.title: WWII In Color: D-Day to Nazi Downfall
programme.desc: After a brutal day of relentless combat, the Allies secure a 50-mile bridgehead in Normandy. Now, American, British, and Canadian forces must push inland, capture a major supply port, and liberate Paris. Facing harsh terrain, supply shortages, and fierce German resistance, casualties soar into the hundreds of thousands in this costly battle for freedom.

programme.title: WWII: Mysteries in the Archives 1938-1948
programme.desc: On Sunday morning, December 7, 1941, Japan declares war on the United States by attacking Pearl Harbor and other American military bases in Hawaii. Why did Japan attack American naval bases in Hawaii? What became of the images shot by John Ford and his team? And how did the censored footage of cameraman John Brick reappear one year later?

programme.title: Battle for Cassino
programme.desc: The Battle For Monte Cassino marked one of the longest and bloodiest engagements of the Italian campaign during World War II. For 9 months, the Allies struggled to take the Gustav Line and the abbey of Monte Cassino. In May 1944, the Gustav Line finally collapsed, with the Second Polish Corps succeeding in capturing the abbey. The Allies had paid a big price, but now the road to Rome was open.

programme.title: The Crusade in the Pacific
programme.desc: This episode focuses on the naval war in the Pacific during World War II. It examines the use of two of the U.S. Navy's most important weapons, the submarine and the aircraft carrier, as well as the supply and mail problems facing U.S. operations in the Pacific. It will provide a glimpse of how is life on board of both these vessels.

programme.title: Sacrifice: From D-Day to the Liberation of Paris
programme.desc: June 6th, 1944, 3 PM: Allies secure beaches; Hitler misjudges, expecting main landings in Pas-de-Calais. Hope rises as French populace anticipates liberation, despite slow Allied progress in Normandy. Paris liberated in August; war persists for another year, marking Normandy's profound sacrifice.

programme.title: Naval Warfare in World War II
programme.desc: In a last effort at glory, having lost most of their best men in military actions, Japan employs suicide pilots - Kamikaze - men who willingly crash their planes into ships in order to destroy the American spirit. But the U.S. Navy and Marines are ready for them with their guns, and they fought heroically against the onslaught. And on Okinawa, Americans fight a major battle with the Japanese Army.

programme.title: World of Warships Clash of Titans
programme.desc: In April 1945, the Yamato, the largest battleship in history, left for Okinawa to destroy American warships and prevent their landing. Weighing 70,000 tonnes and armed with 150 guns, it faced the U.S. naval aviation, including aircraft carriers USS Essex and USS Yorktown. In a fierce battle, American pilots focused on one goal: sink the Yamato. This marked a turning point in WWII naval warfare.

programme.title: The Big Attack: Combat Heroes of WWII
programme.desc: The town of Hotten became very important during WWII as Hitler has ordered it held at all costs because of its key defensive location by the Siegfried Line. An infantry regiment and tanks attack but are stopped by heavy mortar fire. A small squad succeeds by using grenades and .45 submachine guns, allowing the tanks and infantry to take the town after a fierce fight. Stars actor Jim Hutton.

programme.title: Battlezone WWII: The Burma Road Campaign
programme.desc: Allied forces from all over the world combine to liberate Burma from the Japanese occupation in WWII.

programme.title: Military Legends of World War II
programme.desc: Nimitz was Commander in Chief, United States Pacific Fleet and Pacific Ocean Areas on WWII. Promoted to Fleet Admiral in December 1944 he signed for the United States when Japan formally surrendered.

programme.title: The Big Attack: Combat Heroes of WWII
programme.desc: An American Intelligence Officer faces off against a brutal Russian Colonel in a tense story about the 'kidnapping' of fifteen German war orphans. Sheltered by a brave Baroness, the children's fate is threatened when V Day Armistice places her home in the Russian zone. U.S. Captain Tom Ryan and Sergeant Steve Maycheck, decide to rescue the orphans and the Baroness, leading to a thrilling climax.

programme.title: The Third Reich in Color
programme.desc: From 1937, colour films also document life in Hitler's Germany. Eva Braun and Hitler's pilot Hans Baur are among the first amateur filmmakers to expose the new celluloid. This creates unique images of the dictator's public appearances and his private life on Obersalzberg. Scanned in high-resolution HD, the footage of Hitler and his entourage unfolds a particularly realistic effect.

programme.title: The Crusade in Europe
programme.desc: President Roosevelt lectures Americans on their conduct. Churchill visits the U.S. American troops are deployed to England, and Eisenhower gets command of the European Theater of Operations.

programme.title: Patton's Finest Hour: The Battle Of The Bulge
programme.desc: Story of America's winter soldier throughout the history of the country from valley forge to the Battle of the Bulge.

programme.title: Battlezone WWII: Battle of Midway to Victory in the Pacific
